item.title: Roland Releases Melody Flip AI Plugin for DAWs
item.description:
Roland Releases Melody Flip AI Plugin for DAWs

Roland has entered the generative AI music space with Melody Flip, a DAW plug‑in that creates short musical loops to spark creativity.

🔍 Overview

  • Roland’s new Melody Flip tool marks the company’s foray into generative AI music.
  • Available as a plug‑in for digital audio workstations (DAWs).

🧩 How it works

  • Users can start from scratch and ask the plugin to generate any combination of melody, chord progression, bassline, or drums.
  • Alternatively, a reference track can be provided; the tool builds off its melodic ideas.
  • Outputs are simple musical loops intended as a creative spark, not fully polished songs.

⚙️ Features

  • Around 250 “Palettes,” themed collections of musical ideas sorted by genre.
  • Genre selection is fine‑grained: from standard styles like “80s disco” and “90s R&B” to niche categories such as “Kawaii Future Bass” and “Anime World.”
  • Users choose genre, note density, BPM, and key; there is no text‑prompt interface.
  • Preset sounds are basic MIDI tones similar to those found in 1990s video games.
  • Intended workflow: export MIDI data from Melody Flip into a DAW and pair it with more powerful synth plugins.

🚀 Availability

  • The plugin is released for DAWs (no specific platforms are listed in the available evidence).

💡 Why it matters

  • Melody Flip differs from services like Suno or Udio, which output fully arranged songs with vocals.
  • The limited controls and generic sound palette suggest the tool is meant for ideation rather than final production.
  • Given the mixed reception of generative AI in the music community, the plugin is unlikely to generate widespread goodwill.

#Roland #AImusic #MelodyFlip

Source: Roland is getting into generative AI music with Melody Flip

item.title: ARIA bans fully AI-generated songs from official Australian music charts
item.description:
ARIA bans fully AI-generated songs from official Australian music charts

Australia’s official chart body, ARIA, has changed its rules so that recordings created primarily by artificial intelligence are no longer eligible to appear on the ARIA Charts.

🔍 Overview

  • AI‑generated music has pushed the music industry into new territory.
  • While many countries are introducing copyright, transparency and labeling rules, ARIA has taken the most explicit step by drawing a clear line for chart eligibility.

⚙️ Rule specifics

  • The restriction applies when AI is responsible for the main creative performance of a track.
  • Examples of ineligible recordings:
    • A song with an AI‑generated lead vocal.
    • A track where a major instrumental performance is generated by AI.
    • Recordings created almost entirely from AI prompts.
  • AI can still be used for supporting tools such as mastering, stem separation, or other production assistance.
  • The rule does not prevent artists from using AI at all; it only bars fully AI‑created works from chart competition.

🌍 Global context

  • Europe has introduced transparency requirements for AI‑generated content.
  • The UK is discussing copyright and AI training, and the US is moving to protect artists’ voices and identities.
  • Music organisations are adding clearer labeling for AI recordings and setting new chart‑qualification conditions.
  • Spotify plans to display AI Persona badges on artist profiles built around AI identities.
  • Data company Luminate has launched a framework within its CONNECT platform to identify AI‑generated songs and artist profiles, reporting thousands of such recordings already in its database.
  • These initiatives show the industry is shifting from treating AI music as a side note to actively tracking and measuring it.

📊 Impact

  • Despite new rules elsewhere, AI‑generated tracks can still appear on many official charts.
  • ARIA’s rule is currently the clearest line, ensuring that only music with a primary human creative performance competes on its charts.
  • The change may influence other markets to adopt similar eligibility standards.

#AIMusic #MusicIndustry #ARIA #Copyright

Source: AUSTRALIA BECOMES FIRST COUNTRY TO BAN FULLY AI-GENERATED MUSIC FROM OFFICIAL CHARTS - AStepFWD
